newsitem.title: USA: GE's Employers Re sees no near-term takeovers.
newsitem.headline: GE's Employers Re sees no near-term takeovers.

text.p: KANSAS CITY, Dec 9, Reuter - After emerging empty-handed from this summer's reinsurance takeover scramble, Employers Reinsurance Corp is unlikely to attempt another major takeover, top company executives said.
Employers Re chief executive Kaj Ahlmann told Reuters a takeover of one of the remaining reinsurers would not make strategic or financial sense.
He added that Employers Re is not under any pressure from its parent, General Electric Co, to do a deal.

Ahlmann said when he asked GE chairman Jack Welch whether Employers Re might be for sale, Welch responded in a terse handwritten memo, "Absolutely not." Ahlmann added that although Employers Re discusses its plans and projections with GE once a year, it is not required to meet any specific targets to keep GE satisfied.
Ahlmann said Employers Re expects net income growth in 1997 of 13 percent, based on generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). Return on equity is expected to remain around 15 percent, he said.

Employers Re is also unlikely to try to sell or spin off a stake to take advantage of the hot merger market, Ahlmann said during an interview last week. He said Employers Re, the world's third-largest reinsurer and an early player in the acquisition market, will focus now on organic growth, not big deals.
"We're not saying we're unwilling to buy something," Ahlmann said But "our view is that there will be too much overlap.

"It doesn't make strategic sense, or financial sense for that matter, because we will have to pay a full price and it will basically be consolidating acquisitions," he said on Thursday in his Overland Park, Kansas, office.

"Swiss Re (Swiss Reinsurance Co) has a tremendous amount of business in Germany, tremendous amount of business in France for example, but so do we. There's a limit to what we'll pay for it at this stage.
"Years ago we would pay more, but it doesn't make sense anymore," Ahlmann said.
Employers Re executive vice president Alan Mauch agreed.
"What's next for us is organic growth. No more mega-deals for us," Mauch said.
An early player in the acquisition market, Employers Re in 1995 bought Aachen Re Group and a majority stake in Frankona Reinsurance Co, both based in Germany.
Ahlmann said Employers Re this past summer was unwilling to top rival offers for National Re Corp, American Re Corp and M&G Re when the deals turned into auctions.
"We knew exactly what we were willing to pay for those companies that were acquired by somebody else this summer," Ahlmann said.
Mauch said Employers Re was unwilling to overpay to pick up market share.

Employers Re last month denied a rumor that it might sell its operations to Swiss Re. Some in the market had speculated Swiss Re might make an offer for Employers Re to gain market share in the United States, where Swiss Re currently stands fourth in reinsurance.

In an industry that increasingly views bigger as better, Employers Re ranks second in the United States behind General Re Corp and has a dominant presence in the excess casualty and accident and health reinsurance markets.

Ahlmann said he sees potential for future growth in Europe as the governments there are forced to revamp their healthcare systems. The company also plans to expand its Singapore office into a regional headquarters in the first quarter as it positions itself for growth in Asia, Ahlmann said.
Employers Re also may open a regional office in Florida as a springboard into Latin America, he said. The company's other regional headquarters are in Munich and Kansas City.
Meanwhile Employers Re is focusing on special markets and relationships where prices for business tend to remain strong and are less influenced by pricing cycles, he said.
He said the company will emphasize strict underwriting standards and turn away unprofitable business.
"Why put it on the book at a loss?" he asked.

Employers Re also is working to make measurable improvements in the quality of its products and services. He said the company expects a $50 million improvement in profitability by the year 2000 through a program GE launched this year emphasizing measurable improvements quality.
"It's amazing how much you can improve," he said, adding he expects the program to improve long-term profitability through changes in corporate culture.

GE has held financial control of Employers Re since July 1984 when it purchased all of the outstanding capital stock of the company from Texaco Inc. Texaco had received the stock from Getty Oil Co, which it acquired in February 1984.
Ahlmann joined Employers Re in 1988 and was named chief executive in 1993. Before joining Employers Re, he was managing director of Nordisk Reinsurance Co A/S.
Employers Re has a staff of 2,200 worldwide.
